cvpr2023-reconstruction.title: Theorem 1: reconstruct every masked output
cvpr2023-reconstruction.overview: Expand the dividends and exchange finite double sums. Opposite-sign pairing cancels every output coefficient except that of the retained set.
assumptions: Finite universe; the same input, model and input baseline are fixed.

definitions.body_md: Fix a finite universe $N$, input $x$ and input baseline vector $r$. The mask $x_S$ retains the original coordinates in $S$ and uses this same baseline elsewhere. The model is $v:X\to\mathbb R$, the game is $g(S)=v(x_S)$ and the output baseline is $b=g(\varnothing)$. The paper uses raw dividends $w_A=I_g(A)=\sum_{U\subseteq A}(-1)^{|A|-|U|}g(U)$. Every subset sum includes the empty set, so $w_\varnothing=b$. Centering $g_0=g-b$ changes only the empty dividend. A zero raw output baseline is not assumed.

proof_steps.title: Translate the original SCM into one fixed coefficient family
proof_steps.body_md: For a fixed input, model and baseline, $C_A(x_S)=1$ exactly when $A\subseteq S$. The theorem therefore concerns the same coefficients $w_A$ at every $S\subseteq N$. Statistical independence of input variables is not a premise of this finite algebra.

proof_steps.title: Exchange finite sums and cancel each interval
proof_steps.body_md: Expand $w_A$ at fixed $S$. Each pair $L\subseteq A\subseteq S$ occurs once, so exchange the finite sums. For fixed $L$, let $B=A\setminus L\subseteq S\setminus L$, a bijection with $|A|-|L|=|B|$. If $L\ne S$, choose a variable in the difference and pair subsets with and without it; opposite signs cancel. If $L=S$, only empty $B$ remains with coefficient 1. Thus only $g(S)$ survives.

proof_steps.title: Check the empty mask and two variables
proof_steps.body_md: At an empty mask the only term is $w_\varnothing=b$. For mask outputs 7, 8, 9 and 13 on two variables, the dividends are 7, 1, 2 and 3; reconstruction gives full output 13, empty output 7 and singleton outputs 8 and 9.

cvpr2023-uniqueness.title: Appendix C: uniqueness of coefficients reconstructing all masks
cvpr2023-uniqueness.overview: The empty mask fixes the constant coefficient. At each larger set, subtracting the already fixed proper-subset coefficients uniquely determines its coefficient.
assumptions: Finite universe; the same input, model and input baseline are fixed.

cvpr2023-uniqueness.proof_scope: entire original result; source proof and repaired proof separately preserved

proof_steps.title: Keep every mask and one fixed coefficient family
proof_steps.body_md: Assume fixed coefficients $d_A$ reconstruct $g(S)$ for every $S\subseteq N$, including the empty set. An equality only at the full input cannot imply uniqueness.

proof_steps.title: Use strong induction on set cardinality
proof_steps.body_md: The empty set gives $d_\varnothing=g(\varnothing)=w_\varnothing$. The strong induction hypothesis says that every subset with cardinality below $|S|$ has its correct dividend. Every proper subset of $S$ is covered. Subtract the two reconstruction equalities at $S$ after replacing their identical proper-subset terms; the remaining terms give $d_S=w_S$. Since $S$ is arbitrary, all coefficients are unique.

proof_steps.title: Check the empty coefficient and necessary quantifiers
proof_steps.body_md: For outputs 7, 8, 9 and 13, the empty equation fixes coefficient 7, the singleton equations fix 1 and 2, and the full equation fixes 3. If only the full output 13 is required, putting all of 13 at the empty coefficient or all at the full-set coefficient both fit that one equality. Other masks cannot be omitted.

proof_steps.title: Check each binary trigger
proof_steps.body_md: For a retained set $S$, set $X_i=\mathbf1_{i\in S}$. If $A\subseteq S$, every factor in the pattern product is 1; otherwise some factor is zero. The product is therefore exactly the containment indicator. The empty product is 1, so the empty pattern always fires.

proof_steps.title: Retain exactly the activated patterns
proof_steps.body_md: Substitute the trigger identity into the SCM readout for any finite retained pattern family. Every pattern not contained in $S$ contributes zero, so only contained patterns remain. The family need not contain all patterns. When it is the full powerset, reconstruction identifies the sum with $g(S)$.

proof_steps.title: Recompute all dividends for each input baseline
proof_steps.body_md: For each baseline $r$, define all masks and the game $g_r(S)=v(x_S^{(r)})$, then recompute its dividends. Finite reconstruction gives the exact output at every mask. A baseline change requires changing the game and recomputing the coefficients; they generally do change.

proof_steps.title: Each complete squared residual is zero
proof_steps.body_md: Without deleting patterns, each residual between the masked output and its complete dividend sum vanishes. Squaring preserves zero, and the finite sum is zero. Any two baselines satisfy this statement separately. After truncation to a retained pattern family, the theorem no longer guarantees zero residual.

proof_steps.title: Preserve the source sentence’s false truncated-loss interpretation
proof_steps.body_md: If the sentence that a baseline “just affects” the retained coefficients’ L1 norm is read as saying truncated loss is baseline-independent, it is false. For $v(z)=z$, original input 1, input baseline $r$, and only the empty pattern retained, the complete dividends are $r$ and $1-r$. The truncated loss is $(1-r)^2$ and changes with $r$. Complete-dividend loss remains zero. The complete-reconstruction subclaim is proved, while the additional interpretation is not counted as fully verified.
proof_steps.justification: Direct evaluation at the two masks; no training or probability assumption is involved.

proof_steps.title: Combine two child AND triggers
proof_steps.body_md: Containment of $A\cup B$ in $T$ is equivalent to containment of both $A$ and $B$. The union trigger is therefore the product of the two binary triggers. Overlap between the child variable sets is allowed because trigger values are zero or one.

proof_steps.title: Repeated merging preserves each pattern state and the root output
proof_steps.body_md: For a finite child family with variable sets $V_c$, the parent set is their union. Induct over the child family. The empty family gives an empty union and empty product, both with trigger 1. Inserting a child uses the two-set union identity and the induction hypothesis, proving the product identity. Child variables may overlap and a child may be shared by several parents. Applying such a grouping to every original pattern preserves each trigger; retaining its coefficient preserves the weighted root output.

proof_steps.title: Check an empty pattern and a shared-node example
proof_steps.body_md: A shared node with variable set $\{5,6\}$ groups the pattern $\{4,5,6\}$ into children $\{4\}$ and that node. With mask $\{4,5\}$ neither representation fires; with the full pattern mask both fire. The empty pattern and empty child product both have trigger 1. This proves equivalent regrouping only; optimality of the MDL greedy algorithm is separate.

cvpr2023-addmul-coefficients.title: Binary addition–multiplication models: dividends are activated-term coefficients
cvpr2023-addmul-coefficients.overview: Coordinate masking at a zero input baseline turns each monomial into a pure AND response. Linearity then combines its exact dividend; the coefficient includes the original sample product.
assumptions: Binary coordinates and input baseline zero; merge polynomial terms with identical variable sets. A zero input baseline does not imply a zero output baseline for general models.

definitions.body_md: Fix a finite universe $N$, input $x$ and input baseline vector $r$. The mask $x_S$ retains the original coordinates in $S$ and uses this same baseline elsewhere. The model is $v:X\to\mathbb R$, the game is $g(S)=v(x_S)$ and the output baseline is $b=g(\varnothing)$. The paper uses raw dividends $w_A=I_g(A)=\sum_{U\subseteq A}(-1)^{|A|-|U|}g(U)$. Every subset sum includes the empty set, so $w_\varnothing=b$. Centering $g_0=g-b$ changes only the empty dividend. A zero raw output baseline is not assumed.

cvpr2023-addmul-coefficients.proof_scope: entire original result; source proof and repaired proof separately preserved

proof_steps.title: Evaluate each term at the fixed binary sample
proof_steps.body_md: For a monomial at input baseline zero, retaining its entire variable set keeps every factor; otherwise some factor is replaced by zero. Thus the masked monomial equals its coefficient times the original sample product times the containment indicator. An original zero factor makes that coefficient vanish; the empty monomial has product 1. Combine original terms with identical variable sets first.

proof_steps.title: Transform each pure AND response and combine by linearity
proof_steps.body_md: The finite addition–multiplication polynomial, evaluated on actual coordinate masks, is a sum of pure AND games by the preceding identity. Each has a dividend only at its own variable set. Finite linearity therefore makes a fixed set receive precisely its original coefficient times its sample product, if present in the polynomial, and zero otherwise.

proof_steps.title: Check both source samples and the boundary
proof_steps.body_md: The source model is $v(x)=3x_1-2x_2x_3-x_3x_4x_5+5x_4x_6$. At the all-ones sample its nonzero dividends are 3, −2, −1 and 5 at the four displayed monomial sets. When the third coordinate is zero, only dividends 3 and 5 remain. Full outputs are respectively 5 and 8. Both examples have zero empty-mask output and empty dividend; these are exact activated-term coefficients.

cvpr-issue-beta-proof.title: Beta-integral exponent and boundary errors
cvpr-issue-beta-proof.evidence_md: The supplement defines the beta integral for positive parameters but prints exponent 1-q where q-1 is required. At p=1,q=2 the printed integral diverges while its claimed factorial value is finite. Other steps use a zero beta parameter and identify an integral as one at an empty set although its integrand is zero. An extreme empty remaining universe also requires an explicit empty-sum case.
cvpr-issue-beta-proof.impact_md: These are errors in the proofs of the factorial coefficients, not counterexamples to Theorems 2–4. The repaired finite convolution proves the original conclusions, including boundary cases, without introducing integral domain assumptions.

cvpr-issue-distribution-incomparable.title: The distribution proof omits incomparable sets
cvpr-issue-distribution-incomparable.evidence_md: The printed cases of a target strictly below, equal to, or strictly above the unanimity field omit incomparable sets. For universe {1,2}, field {1}, and target {2}, no subset of the target contains the field, so every summand is zero. The complete partition is: the field is not contained in the target; the two are equal; or the field is strictly contained in the target.
cvpr-issue-distribution-incomparable.impact_md: The original distribution proposition remains true. The repair fills the missing case without changing its quantifiers and also supplies the Add/Mul application.

cvpr-issue-lagrange-equivalence.title: Unjustified equivalence with a penalized objective
cvpr-issue-lagrange-equivalence.evidence_md: The source converts constrained sparsity minimization to a penalized problem without choosing a multiplier or establishing a suitable equivalence. In a generic discrete optimization example with (support,error) pairs (0,3),(1,2),(2,0), a budget of one selects the middle point, but making it minimize error plus multiplier times support requires the multiplier to be both at most one and at least two.
cvpr-issue-lagrange-equivalence.impact_md: This example establishes the failure of generic equivalence, without claiming that the three points are realized by the paper’s DNN. The source conversion remains a heuristic; the missing model-specific equivalence is not supplied as an assumption.

cvpr-issue-ratio-zero-denominator.title: The retained-effect ratio has an unspecified zero denominator
cvpr-issue-ratio-zero-denominator.evidence_md: The ratio divides retained absolute effects by retained absolute effects plus the absolute remainder. A zero game has all these quantities zero, giving the undefined expression 0/0.
cvpr-issue-ratio-zero-denominator.impact_md: No value is invented for this boundary case. Finite reconstruction and uniqueness are unaffected; this issue concerns the displayed diagnostic ratio.

cvpr-issue-baseline-truncated-loss.title: The baseline can change the truncated unfaithfulness loss
cvpr-issue-baseline-truncated-loss.evidence_md: For the identity model, input one and baseline r, the full dividends are r and 1-r. Retaining only the empty coalition gives squared reconstruction error (1-r)^2, which varies with the baseline. Full reconstruction still has zero error for every baseline.
cvpr-issue-baseline-truncated-loss.impact_md: The full-coefficient zero-loss clause is true, but the claim that the baseline affects only the sparsity term is false for a truncated family. The compound sentence is not weakened and then marked proved.
